Sam — thanks for the profile, that helps a lot. Quick read here and an initial proposal below; looping in Grace (SE) for technical fit and Neha (pricing) for term options.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Hybrid commit: baseline L40S capacity sized to cover steady-state embeddings and lower-cost gen (70% of sustained token volume).
- H100 reserved slab for peak real-time generation (30% capacity + 10% flex buffer for short bursts).
- Commit options: 12-month (moderate discount) or 24-month (steeper discount + SLA uplift).

Why this split: L40S gives best perf/$ for throughput-oriented workloads (embeddings and short completions) because of better memory density per $ and lower hourly price; H100 gives lower latency for long-context generation and better throughput at large batch sizes for top-tier latency-sensitive routes. You get unit-cost savings by placing predictable bulk volume on L40S but keep latency-sensitive tails on H100.

I'll attach a draft term sheet with concrete numbers and a simple sample invoice. Grace — can you validate our memory/kv-cache assumptions for your models? Neha — I'll need the price matrix for 12 vs 24 month on both SKUs.

Next steps: propose we run a 2-week pilot with a small H100 burst pool and L40S baseline to validate tail latencies and perf/$ curves before committing. Open to procurement timelines — Sam, does that sequencing work?

Best,
Dylan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Sam / Dylan — dug into the attached demand profile. A few technical clarifications and constraints so pricing assumptions are realistic: 

1) Model footprints: your production generation model (2.4B / 8k context) will fit comfortably on 48GB A100 and on H100-80GB; L40S (48GB variant) is fine for the 2.4B but tight if you move to 8k context with large KV cache retention. If you anticipate growing to 16k contexts we should allocate more H100s or A100-80GB variants.

2) KV cache behavior: embeddings-heavy batch jobs benefit from L40S memory density; realtime gen that relies on long KV caches benefits from H100 due to better memory bandwidth and multi-stream performance.

3) Perf/$ roughs (back-of-envelope, normalized):
- L40S: best perf/$ for embeddings and smaller latency-insensitive completions.
- H100: ~25-35% higher throughput for long-context generation vs L40S but ~40-60% higher hourly cost depending on region and memory variant.

4) Suggested config for your numbers:
- Baseline commit: 40 L40S GPUs (covers ~70% steady volume)
- Reserved H100 slab: 12 H100-80GB (covers peak gen tail + 10% flex buffer)
- Burst credits: an additional 10 L40S-equivalent burst credits you can draw at reduced short-term rate (30% uplift vs committed price) for unexpected spikes.

I'll prepare a latency table (p95, p99) for the two-sku mix with your sample traffic. Markus — if we offer a hard p99 latency SLA for the gen route we need a pricing uplift (in my estimate +8-12% on the overall commit).

-Grace
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — attaching the draft term sheet (Redwood_Hybrid_Commit_Term_Sheet.pdf) but summarizing key commercials inline to speed review: 

Offer A (12-month):
- 40 x L40S committed: list $/GPU-hr -> discounted to 15% off list; included baseline throughput guarantees (SLA: 99.5% availability per month on committed pool).
- 12 x H100-80GB reserved: 12-month commit, 18% off list.
- Flex buffer / burst credits: 10% of committed capacity available monthly billed at committed rate + 30% uplift; unused burst credits do not roll over.
- No automatic refund; credits can be applied to future invoice within same 12-month term if usage falls below forecast > but not pro-rata refunds.

Offer B (24-month):
- 40 x L40S committed: 22% off list.
- 12 x H100-80GB reserved: 28% off list + optional p99 SLA uplift at +10% on top of committed price (if DataForge purchases SLA, we commit to p99 latency for gen route with a 5% service credit on missed SLOs).
- Flex buffer: 10% with rollover up to 1 month and billed at committed rate + 20% uplift.
- Cancellation: 6-month notice window; pro-rata refund on unused committed dollars after 6 months only in the event of structural force majeure or portfolio shutdown — otherwise standard early-termination fee (10% of remaining committed value).

We're open to negotiating the cancellation language but need to protect capacity planning. If you prefer true pro-rata refunds we can price that into the deal but it will increase unit prices by ~5-8% across the board.

-Neha
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — the two offers are clear and appreciated. A few clarifying points before we turn to legal: 

1) For Offer B (24-month), the rollover of flex buffer up to 1 month is attractive. Can we expand that to allow one-time rollover of up to 25% of a single month’s unused burst to the end-of-term credit? That would give us flexibility for seasonal spikes.

2) For the SLA uplift: if we take the +10% SLA uplift, what are the remediation timelines (incident response and root-cause windows)? Also please confirm measurement window for p99 (30-day rolling).

3) Cancellation: procurement will push for a softer early-termination remedy (pro-rata refund after 3 months) — if you can’t do that, can we get a cap on the early-termination fee (max $200k)?

If you can update the term sheet with these three items we can route to legal. Otherwise this looks in line with expectations. We like the hybrid approach — keeps our unit cost down while preserving peak gen latency.

—Sam
Head of Platform, DataForge Inc
